lines.text: אהר 37 אהר
Note. Instead of the sing. אַחַר, the
plur. אַחֲרֵי is far more frequently used;
see below. With suffixes the plur. form
is always used.
Plur. אֲחָרִים, only in constr. אַחֲרֵי, c.
suff. אַחֲרַי, אַחֲרֵיכֶם, אַחֲרֵיהֶם, etc.
1. Subst. the hinder parts, 2 Sam. 2,
23 בְּאַחֲרֵי הַחֲנִית with the hinder end of
the spear.
2. Prep. a) Of place, behind, Judg.
18, 12 where it is i. q. on the west of, see
in אָחוֹר no. 2. More freq. after, behind
any one, Lev. 26, 33. 1 Sam. 14, 37.
2 K. 19, 21. (אֲשֶׁר) אַחֲרֵיהֶם those who
go after them, their flatterers, parasites,
Ps. 49, 14. Hence, with verbs of going,
to follow; also הָיָה אַחֲרֵי פ׳ to be after,
to go after any one, i. q. to follow, to be
on one’s side, Ex. 23, 2. 2 Sam. 2, 10.
Comp. 1 K. 1, 7. Prov. 28, 23 מוֹכִיחַ אָדָם
אַחֲרַי חֵן יִמְצָא he that rebuketh a man
after me (i. e. after my precepts) shall
find favour. b) Of time, after, Gen.
16, 13. 17, 8. With inf. after that, after,
3. Conj. אַחֲרֵי אֲשֶׁר after that, Deut.
24, 4. Josh. 9, 16. 23, 1; rarely with אֲשֶׁר
omitted, Lev. 25, 48. Once אַחֲרֵי כַּאֲשֶׁר
Josh. 2, 7.
4. אַחֲרֵי־כֵן pr. after so, after it had so
happened, i. e. afterwards, Gen. 6, 4.
ܒܳܬܰܪܟܶܢ and ܒܳܬܰܪ ܗܳܟܰܢ. With אֲשֶׁר added
it becomes a conjunction, i. q. אַחֲרֵי אֲשֶׁר
after that, like Lat. posteaquam for post-
quam, Deut. 24, 4. 2 Sam. 24, 10. In the
later Hebrew we find also אַחֲרֵי זֹאת
after this, afterwards, Job 42, 16. Ezra
9, 10. Comp. Chald. אַחֲרֵי דְנָה Dan. 2,
5. With other prepositions:
a) מֵאַחֲרֵי, once מִן אַחֲרֵי 1 Chr. 17, 7,
pr. from after, from behind, from going
or following after; chiefly used of those
who abandon a person or party whom
they have before followed, Num. 14, 43.
Deut. 7, 4. 2 Sam. 20, 2. Also at or on
the back, behind, after, (comp. מִן no. 3.
Of time, after, Ecc. 10, 14; and in Neh.
4, 7 מֵאַחֲרֵי לְ, in the same sense. Hence
מֵאַחֲרֵי כֵן pr. after so, i. e. afterwards,
b) אֶל־אַחֲרֵי after, with verbs of mo-
tion. 2 K. 9, 18 סֹב אֶל־אַחֲרַי turn thee
after me, behind me, 2 Sam. 5, 23.
c) עַל־אַחֲרֵי i. q. אַחֲרֵי, Ez. 41, 15.
Comp. עַל no. 3. b.
אַחַר Chald. plur. constr. אַחֲרֵי, after,
Dan. 2, 29; but by Hebraism. The
pure Chaldee preposit. is בָּתַר.
אַחֲרוֹן, fem. אַחֲרֹנָה, from אַחַר with
the adj. ending וֹן.
1. hinder, hindermost, latter, opp. to
foremost, former, (רִאשׁוֹן,) Gen. 33, 2.
Ex. 4, 8. Deut. 24, 3. הַיָּם הָאַחֲרוֹן the
hinder sea, i. e. western, the Mediterra-
nean, Deut. 11, 24. 34, 2. Joel 2, 20.
2. after, later, following, as דּוֹר אַחֲרוֹן
Ps. 48, 14. יוֹם אַחֲרוֹן after time, future,
Prov. 31, 25. Is. 30, 8. Plur. אַחֲרֹנִים
those after, posterity, Job 18, 20.
3. the last, latest, Neh. 8, 18. Is. 44, 6
I [Jehovah] am the first, and I the last.
Job 19, 25.—Fem. אַחֲרֹנָה adv. last, the
last, Dan. 11, 29. Also בָּאַחֲרֹנָה Deut.
31. Ecc. 1, 11, at last, last.
אַחְרַח (for אַחְרְאַח, after the brother,)
Aharah, pr. n. 1 Chr. 8, 1.
אֲחַרְחֵל (behind the breast-work sc.
born) Aharhel, pr. n. m. 1 Chr. 4, 8.
אַחֲרֵי Chald. constr. see אַחַר Chald.
אָחֳרִי Chald. adj. fem. another, alia,
Dan. 2, 39. 7, 5. 6; for the common
אָחֳרִית, the ת of the fem. gender being
dropped by apocope, like רֵאשִׁי for
רֵאשִׁית, מַלְכוּ for מַלְכוּת.
אָחֳרֵין Chald. adj. (fr. אַחַר הֵן) Dan.
4, 5 עַד־אָחֳרֵין pr. at the last, at last, at
length; the עַד being pleonastic, see עַד
Chald. A. 2.—Keri אָחֳרָן.
אַחֲרִית f. (r. אָחַר) 1. the last or
extreme part, uttermost part, Ps. 139, 9.
—Oftener of time: a) the end of a pe-
riod, Deut. 11, 12; the end, event of any
course of things, latter state, final lot,
Job 8, 7. 42, 12. Prov. 5, 4 אַחֲרִיתָהּ מָרָה
her end is bitter, i. e. the final lot of
those whom the adultress seduces;
comp. 23, 32. Sometimes of a happy
end or result, Prov. 23, 18. 24, 14. b)
after-time, the future, espec. in the pro-
phetic formula בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים in future
time, in the last days, Is. 2, 2. Gen. 49, 1.

line_status.note: Only the order differs. Printed visual order left→right is אַחֲרֵיהֶם then (אֲשֶׁר); as one RTL run the rightmost (אֲשֶׁר) is logically first, giving Reading A's order (אֲשֶׁר) אַחֲרֵיהֶם. Reading B puts the parenthesis logically second, which would render visually reversed. All vowel points, shin dot and the yod in אַחֲרֵיהֶם are as both readings have them.
In the parenthetical form the print has shva (vertical dots) under ח and under ר, and a plain patach (not qamets) under the second א; Reading A's hataf-patach, tsere and qamets are not printed.

Printed left-to-right order is רֵאשִׁית (leftmost, after the comma-separated pair) … for מַלְכוּת (rightmost); Reading A swaps the first and last words. Vowel points agree with both readings; the line also ends with a full stop after מַלְכוּת.
